items.title: Pregnant Inmate Escapes in Prison Vehicle After Medical Appointment
items.summary:
Law enforcement in New Mexico is searching for a pregnant inmate after she escaped while being transported back to prison from a prenatal medical appointment.

The New Mexico Corrections Department announced in a press release on Wednesday, November 25, that Rebecca Taylor fled while officers were driving back to the Western New Mexico Correctional Facility following the appointment in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

“During transport, Taylor was able to take control of the vehicle and drive away,” the department said in the statement.

Taylor, 26, escaped just after 11:30 a.m. when the three-officer team made a stop at a Whataburger in Albuquerque, according to KOAT .

Women on Death Row in the U.S.: Maternal Instinct's Taylor Parker and More 

The driver left the vehicle during the pit stop, and Taylor – who was unrestrained due to her pregnancy – managed to unbuckle herself and moved to the driver’s seat before she drove off.

Another female inmate was also in the vehicle and was able to exit, though she was ultimately taken back into custody.

Authorities used a GPS to eventually find the Dodge Journey transport vehicle near Crestview Drive SW in Albuquerque. The department said that Taylor was not inside the vehicle when it was found.

The search for Taylor continued, and her prison jumpsuit was found discarded at an intersection on Albuquerque’s west side, according to NBC News .

Two hours later, authorities discovered a transport cellphone near a park in southwest Albuquerque, per KOB 4 .
